title: Key Case on AI Training Data Copyright Disputes: Indian Court Supports Legality of Model Training Discussions

content_html:
On July 24, an Indian court ruled in a copyright dispute between the news agency ANI and OpenAI, determining that OpenAI's use of ANI news content for training artificial intelligence models does not constitute copyright infringement, and confirmed that the Indian court has jurisdiction over the case.

This case originated from ANI, one of India's largest news agencies, which had previously sued OpenAI, accusing it of using its news reports without authorization to train AI models and requesting restrictions on the use of related data. During the trial, the Indian court found that ANI failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove that its original news content actually appeared in ChatGPT-generated responses, and therefore did not support its claim of copyright infringement.

The court also confirmed that, although OpenAI is headquartered in the United States, since ChatGPT services are available in India, the related copyright dispute falls within the jurisdiction of the Indian court. This means that the Indian judicial system will continue to participate in discussions on data usage rules between global AI companies and content providers.

In recent years, issues regarding the copyright of AI training data have become a major focal point of controversy in the global artificial intelligence industry. Content producers, including news agencies, publishers, and photo companies, generally pay attention to whether generative AI companies should obtain permission before using publicly available content for model training; while AI companies argue that large-scale data learning is an essential foundation for model capabilities.

Previously, copyright lawsuits related to AI training data have emerged in regions such as the United States and Europe. Although India's ruling does not fully resolve the rules for AI training data copyrights, it provides new judicial references for related disputes.

As large models continue to develop, how to balance AI innovation, data utilization efficiency, and content creators' rights will remain an issue that needs to be continuously addressed in the commercialization process of the global AI industry.

content_html_zh:
7月24日，印度一家法院就新闻机构ANI与OpenAI之间的版权纠纷作出裁决，认定OpenAI利用ANI新闻内容训练人工智能模型的行为不构成版权侵权，并确认印度法院对此案拥有管辖权。

此案起源于印度最大新闻机构之一的 ANI 此前曾起诉 OpenAI，指控其未经授权使用其新闻报道来训练 AI 模型，并要求限制相关数据的使用。 印度法院在审理过程中认为，ANI 未能提供足够的证据证明其原创新闻内容确实出现在 ChatGPT 生成的回复中，因此不支持其侵犯版权的主张。

法院还确认，虽然OpenAI总部位于美国，但由于ChatGPT服务在印度提供，因此相关版权纠纷属于印度法院的管辖范围。 这意味着印度司法系统将继续参与全球AI公司与内容提供商之间数据使用规则的讨论。

近年来，人工智能训练数据的版权问题成为全球人工智能行业争议的一大焦点。 内容生产者，包括新闻机构、出版商、图片公司等，普遍关注生成式AI公司在使用公开内容进行模型训练之前是否应获得许可；而人工智能公司则认为大规模数据学习是模型能力的重要基础。

此前，美国、欧洲等地区已出现与AI训练数据相关的版权诉讼。 印度的裁决虽然没有完全解决人工智能训练数据版权的规则，但为相关纠纷提供了新的司法参考。

随着大模型的不断发展，如何平衡人工智能创新、数据利用效率和内容创作者权益，仍将是全球人工智能产业商业化进程中需要持续解决的问题。
